Top hits of Analyses

Source: R/tophits.R
og_tophits.Rd

Returns each Analysis's Associations at or below a p-value threshold, strongest first, up to limit per Analysis. The query runs as a Job on the API, and og_tophits() waits for it (see vignette("large-queries-and-jobs")).

Usage

og_tophits(
  src,
  analyses,
  threshold = 5e-08,
  limit = 1000,
  observed_only = FALSE,
  clump = TRUE,
  ld = NULL,
  r2 = NULL,
  kb = NULL,
  original_units = FALSE,
  releases = NULL
)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api().

analyses

Analysis identifiers (see og_analyses()).

threshold

The largest p-value to return. Each GWAS Store indexes 5e-8, 5e-6 and 5e-4 and refuses a looser one (opengwasr_unsupported_threshold).

limit

The most top hits to return per Analysis, at most 10,000.

observed_only

Leave out Imputed Associations.

clump

Clump the top hits to one per independent signal.

ld

An LD Store's name, an ancestry code (its LD Store), a PLINK Reference from og_plink_reference(), or NULL to match each Analysis's Assigned Ancestry. Only with clump = TRUE.

r2, kb

The r² above which a top hit joins an index variant's clump, and the window in kilobases; NULL for the LD Store's t_far and far window, but required with a PLINK Reference. Only with clump = TRUE.

original_units

Give beta and se in the trait's original units: Analyses stored per SD are multiplied by their recorded phenotype SD (original_sd), and log-odds Analyses are unchanged. It refuses, with class opengwasr_original_units_unavailable and before any query runs, when an Analysis is stored per SD and isn't a continuous trait with an original_sd; ids and reason on the error say which and why.

releases

Store Releases to use, as in og_analyses().

Value

A data frame with the columns above and og_provenance() attached.

Details

By default (clump = TRUE) the top hits are clumped on the API, one index variant per independent signal (see vignette("ld")): every top hit at threshold is clumped, and limit then caps the index variants. Each Analysis is clumped in the LD Store matching its Assigned Ancestry, or in the one ld names; an Unassigned Analysis is refused (opengwasr_ld_unmatched) unless ld is given, before any Job runs. The Jobs, one per Analysis, are submitted grouped by LD Store; with progress on (option opengwasr.progress), a message of class opengwasr_clumping says which LD Store each Analysis is clumped in. r2 and kb default to the LD Store's Far Threshold (t_far) and its far window (far_bp, 10,000 kb), and are always sent. A pair the LD Store can't answer exactly is refused by the API (opengwasr_ld_refusal). Top hits the LD Store doesn't hold can't be clumped: they are left out, with a warning of class opengwasr_clump_absent (count). Clumped rows add clump_ld, clump_ld_choice, clump_r2, clump_kb and clump_size, and og_provenance(x)$clump has each Analysis's hits, absent and leads. Pass clump = FALSE for every top hit.

With a PLINK Reference in ld (see og_plink_reference()) the clumping is local: each Analysis's top hits are fetched unclumped (up to the API's most, 10,000), matched to the reference by rsID (those not in it are left out, with a message) and clumped by PLINK, and limit is then applied to its index variants. If the API cut an Analysis's top hits off at 10,000, you get an opengwasr_truncated warning that clumping saw only the strongest; clumping on the server (an LD Store in ld) has no such cap. og_provenance(x)$clump names the reference's path and the r2 and kb.

The columns are those the vignette section "What the columns mean" lists: the Analysis id, the variant, beta (z * se), se, z, pval, effect_scale ("sd" or "log_or" from the Analysis's stored effect scale, or "original" with original_units = TRUE), n, sample_size_kind, ncase and ncontrol, association_status and the store_id and release_id each Association came from. n is the Association's own sample size where the API sends one, otherwise the Analysis's sample_size; the other three describe the Analysis. pval underflows to 0 when |z| is above about 38.5; z stays exact, so rank the strongest signals by abs(z).

One Job takes at most 100 Analyses from 10 GWAS Stores, and at most 100,000 rows (limit times its Analyses). A larger request is split into several Jobs, run a few at a time (og_api(max_in_flight = )) and put back together: you get the rows an unsplit request would give, with every Job in og_provenance(). The rows are ordered by Analysis, in the order you asked for, and within each Analysis in the API's order (strongest first), whether one Job or several answered. limit applies to each Analysis, so splitting never changes it. A request the API refuses as too costly (opengwasr_request_too_large) is never split to get round that.

When limit cuts any Analysis's top hits off, you get a warning of class opengwasr_truncated, and og_provenance() has truncated = TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
top <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", clump = FALSE, limit = 10)
og_provenance(top)
} # }
